title: County of Poitou
capsule: The County of Poitou in west-central France was one of the great Carolingian-era marches, held from the tenth century by the Ramnulfid counts who also styled themselves Dukes of Aquitaine. After Eleanor of Aquitaine's marriage to Henry II of England in 1152, Poitou became an Angevin possession; the Wikidata attestation from 1206 corresponds to King John's loss of northern Poitou to Philip II Augustus of France following the conquest of Normandy and the Battle of Bouvines aftermath. English kings retained a rump claim to southern Poitou and Gascony; Louis VIII of France formally attached Poitou to the royal domain in 1224, with the county extinguished as an independent unit by 1250.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Poitou's extent is broadly documented through French royal and English chancery records, though the shifting Angevin-Capetian frontier in the early thirteenth century makes precise year-by-year boundaries approximate.
